rektion: etw. (Akk.) umschreiben (einen Text, das Ende, die Geschichte umschreiben)
definition_de: einen Text neu oder anders schreiben, weil er nicht gut genug war (Ich musste die Einleitung dreimal umschreiben.); übertragen: Geschichte umschreiben. Untrennbar (umschréiben, hat umschrieben) heißt es 'etwas mit anderen Worten beschreiben, ohne es direkt zu nennen'.
example_de: Nach dem Feedback ihrer Lehrerin schrieb Lea den ganzen Aufsatz noch einmal um.
example_en: After her teacher's feedback, Lea rewrote the whole essay once more.
visual_idea: Collocation 'einen Text umschreiben': a teenager at her desk, an old draft covered in big red correction marks pushed aside, crumpled paper balls around the bin, and she writes a fresh page with determination. The old marked draft next to the new page shows 'rewrite', not just 'schreiben'. Handwriting is kept to faint grey lines because paper attracts fake text. Typing on a laptop was rejected because it reads as 'tippen'.
image_prompt: a teenage girl at a wooden desk in her bedroom in the evening, writing with determination on a fresh sheet with a pen, beside her an old handwritten draft pushed aside and covered with big red crosses and red circles, several crumpled paper balls on the desk and around an overflowing small wastepaper bin, all handwriting shown only as faint illegible grey wavy lines, desk lamp light, medium shot
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: a teenage girl looks at an old draft covered in red marks, crumples it into a ball, throws it toward the bin, takes a fresh sheet and starts writing with determination; static medium shot, warm desk lamp light
